_meta.description: probe wire frames: StepperProbe, DCProbe, ChuckPositioner
_meta.captured_from: src/ (the old code), driven in simulator mode
_meta.handshake_note: Transport ping traffic (b's\n') is filtered out of every frame list and counted here. Simulator mode never runs the handshake at all, so this is 0; a non-zero value means a capture was taken against a live port and the pings were removed from the golden bytes.

scenarios.description: Operator arms the probe. `_arm` sends the energize byte, then `_transition`'s quiesce sends a zeroed motion frame so the board starts from rest.
new_calls: probe.run("set_mode", args=(ProbeMode.IDLE,))

decode.text: control byte 'e' (0x65) - energize. Handled by stepper/chuck firmware; falls through to text on the DC board (SERIAL-10).

scenarios.description: Enter AUTONOMOUS (one zeroed frame from the quiesce), then one step. `macro_start_auton` transitions with quiesce=False, so the move frame is the only write it adds - no stop-then-go hiccup at the board.
prelude: <motion parameters written while IDLE; a write to one is refused once AUTONOMOUS or MANUAL (DC-6)>
new_calls: probe.run("set_mode", args=(ProbeMode.AUTO,))
probe.run("step", inputs=<motion parameters>)

scenarios.description: A second step while already AUTONOMOUS. One move frame and nothing else: step stays available while AUTO so repeated stepping works (DC-6, review finding 5).
new_calls: probe.run("step", inputs=<motion parameters>)

scenarios.description: Enter MANUAL from IDLE. Already armed, so no energize byte; the quiesce frame is the whole of it.
new_calls: probe.run("set_mode", args=(ProbeMode.MANUAL,))

scenarios.description: One 42-byte jog packet for the 'neutral' gamepad state. Triggers are remapped from [-1, 1] to [0, 1] and combined as (L - R); bumpers combine as (L - R).
new_calls: probe._send_jog(<levels>)  # driven by Probe._jog_loop, was BaseProbe._input_loop

scenarios.description: The single zeroed jog frame `_input_loop` sends when manual mode ends or the input gate closes (I-4.2). Called with an empty dict, so every field comes from the transport's own defaults - the bytes must match the 'neutral' levels frame exactly.
new_calls: probe._send_jog({})

scenarios.description: Stop motion, then de-energize. The zeroed frame goes first and the 'd' is sent even if it raised - de-energizing is never skipped because an earlier step failed.
new_calls: probe.run("set_mode", args=(ProbeMode.DISABLED,))

decode.text: control byte 'd' (0x64) - de-energize, TOFF=0 on all three TMC2209 drivers. The DC board has no handler; it reads as text and produces a halt, not a de-energize (SERIAL-10).

scenarios.description: FULL STOP: zeroed motion frame, 'd', then 'k\n' - in that order, all on the priority lane. `emergency_stop()` latches and then runs exactly this on a worker, so the byte sequence is the same; it is captured synchronously here so the capture is deterministic.
old_calls: # probe.emergency_stop() sends the same three frames
new_calls: probe._halt_hardware()
# probe.run("estop") -> Model.estop() -> _halt_hardware() on a worker

decode.text: control byte 'd' (0x64) - de-energize, TOFF=0 on all three TMC2209 drivers. The DC board has no handler; it reads as text and produces a halt, not a de-energize (SERIAL-10).
control byte 'k' (0x6B) + LF - coil kill. **No firmware on any board has a handler for this.** It is sent unchanged because this is a stop path; making it real is owner decision D-7.
